question: What does ASCII stand for?

options.text: American Standard Code for Internet Information
Asian Schema Code for Information Interchange
American Standard Code for Information Interchange
Asian Standard Code for Internet Interchange

solution:
The correct answer is __**American Standard Code for Information Interchange**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **American Standard Code for Information Interchange (ASCII)** is a character encoding standard for electronic communication.
 
• ASCII codes represent text in computers, telecommunications equipment, and other devices that use text.
 
• Each letter, digit, or symbol is assigned a number from 0 to 127.
 
• For example, the ASCII code for uppercase **A** is **65**, and for lowercase **a** is **97**.
 
• It was developed from telegraph code and first published as a standard in 1963.
 
• ASCII is now largely replaced by Unicode, which includes ASCII as a subset.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ASCII** originally used 7 bits to represent each character, allowing for 128 unique symbols.
 
• Extended ASCII uses 8 bits, allowing for 256 symbols, which includes additional characters for graphical symbols and foreign language letters.
 
• ASCII has been incorporated into many other coding schemes, such as UTF-8, which is compatible with ASCII and can represent any character in the Unicode standard.
 
• The widespread adoption of ASCII has ensured that text files can be easily shared and understood across different types of computer systems.
